runtime_cross_check.error_summary: MatMul8bitLtBackward returned a view that PEFT attempts to modify in place; PyTorch forbids replacing a custom-function backward through view mutation.

source_root_cause_chain.fact: The int8 LoRA forward obtains the quantized base output from super().forward(x), computes the scaled LoRA branch, then mutates the custom-function output through result += output.
Linear8bitLt.forward returns the result of bnb.matmul, without cloning that returned tensor.
MatMul8bitLt.forward retains original input_shape; for the 3D LLaMA input it returns output.reshape(output_shape), a view produced inside the custom autograd Function.

The IN_CUSTOM_FUNCTION branch rejects view mutations that would override the custom backward; it points to differentiable cloning as one remedy. This guard is observed in the current2.6 stack; no claim that it first appeared in2.6.

Reentrant checkpoint runs initial forward under no_grad and repeats the function with grad enabled during backward. This explains why the real forward/loss can succeed while the same in-place expression fails in backward recomputation.

first_choice_for_future_explicit_authori.choice: Retain the current pinned environment and all already-approved settings. In isolated derived PEFT0.5 int8 forward code replace only the LoRA residual mutation with out-of-place addition.
first_choice_for_future_explicit_authori.why_first: Avoids mutating the custom-function view while preserving the original quantized base call, LoRA branch, scaling, dropout invocation, parameter objects, initialization RNG, data, temperature/loss, mask, global64 and checkpointing. Keeps the new change smaller than another dependency-version switch.
first_choice_for_future_explicit_authori.implementation_boundary: Do not edit the installed wheel or author vendor source. A saved derived forward must retain the original base-call semantics and all branch/dtype behavior, with a reviewable source diff and source/version guards. Binding a copied standalone method must handle the original zero-argument super closure correctly; do not assume copying its text is sufficient.
first_choice_for_future_explicit_authori.mathematical_gradient_definition: For R = base(x) + scaling*B(A(dropout(x))), out-of-place addition leaves the ordinary derivative of each summed branch equal to the incoming gradient. The base parameters remain frozen, but its input gradient must still flow to upstream LoRA and saved embeddings.
first_choice_for_future_explicit_authori.precision_limit: The proposal changes tensor aliasing/storage, not the intended sum or scalar hyperparameters. Forward rounding and actual autograd/ZeRO behavior still require measurement; historical bitwise equivalence is not claimed.
first_choice_for_future_explicit_authori.alternative_same_method: A differentiable result.clone() before the in-place residual addition also avoids mutating the custom output and preserves an identity gradient edge; it adds a copy. Never use detach(), .data manipulation or no_grad to bypass this failure.

secondary_static_option.fact: Uses result = result + output and casts non-AMP input to the actual LoRA A weight dtype. It statically avoids the two observed old-PEFT dtype/view issues.
secondary_static_option.tradeoffs: Additional hub/dependency checks and changed wrapper construction/RNG consumption; same initialization distribution does not guarantee same seed42 parameter tensors. Still needs legacy bnb state-field compatibility and actual gradient/save/reload validation.
